usageNotes: Use this to register a new Active Directory realm in Proxmox Datacenter Manager so PDM-managed nodes can authenticate users against your AD/LDAP server. Requires the `Realm.Allocate` privilege on the `access/domains` ACL path — API tokens are accepted. The realm name must be unique across all realms and cannot be changed after creation; set `bind-dn` and `password` if the AD server requires authenticated binds.

examples.summary: Create a corporate AD realm with LDAPS, authenticated bind, and attribute sync

tips: The `realm` value becomes part of every synced user's login name (user@realm) and cannot be renamed — choose it carefully before first use.
Use `mode: ldaps` with `port: 636` and `verify: true` for production; the default `ldap` on port 389 sends credentials in plaintext.
If your AD enforces authenticated queries, `bind-dn` and `password` are effectively required even though the spec marks them optional.
After creating the realm, trigger a user sync via the corresponding sync endpoint to populate PDM users from the AD directory.
Setting `default: true` makes this realm pre-selected on the PDM login page — only one realm should have this flag.
